title: Module objects
statement: Let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative ring object of a symmetric monoidal category $\mathscr C$. An $\mathcal R$-module is an object $M$ of $\mathscr C$ with a unital associative action $\mathcal R\otimes M\to M$, the associativity and unit isomorphisms of $\mathscr C$ being included in these identities. Morphisms are action-preserving morphisms of $\mathscr C$. Write $\mathsf{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathscr C)$ for this category. For $\mathscr C=\mathsf{Sh}(X_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$ write $\mathsf{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(X_{\Proet})$, and for $\mathcal R=\mathcal R_{X,T}$ also $\mathsf{Mod}(X_{\Proet},T)$.

proof.text: The commutative ring-object node identifies $\mathcal R$ with a monoid object in the symmetric monoidal category $\mathscr C$. Applying the existing module-object definition to this monoid object gives objects $M$ with an action $\mathcal R\otimes M\to M$ satisfying the unit and associativity equations (with the associator and unitor), action-preserving morphisms, and the category $\mathsf{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathscr C)$.

proof.text: For any scheme $X$, use the symmetric monoidal structure on $\mathscr C=\mathsf{Sh}(X_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$ specified in [pur713-def-ring-object]. For an arbitrary commutative ring object $\mathcal R$ in this category, the construction in step 1 is denoted $\mathsf{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(X_{\Proet})$. For the further abbreviation, fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its valuation topology, a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $T\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ as in [pur713-def-coefficient-rings]. That node supplies $\mathcal R_{X,T}=p_X^*\underline T$ as a commutative ring object of exactly this sheaf category. Set $\mathcal R=\mathcal R_{X,T}$ in the preceding construction and write $\mathsf{Mod}(X_{\Proet},T)$ for the resulting category.

lean.note: Use CategoryTheory.Mod C R.X for R : CategoryTheory.CommMon C in a symmetric monoidal category C, with the canonical tensor selfLeftAction. ModObj supplies the unital associative action including the left unitor and associator, and Mod.Hom supplies precisely action-preserving morphisms. For arbitrary R in CommMon (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}), use Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}) R.X. For Mod(X_Proet,T), take R.X = (AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.coefficientRing X (Mon.mk Lambda)).X with Lambda equal to Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ell E, Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E, or Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ell, respectively. These are exactly the three inputs of the recorded pur713-def-coefficient-rings declaration; E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ell and [Fact ell.Prime]. Thus every specialization is an application of the existing definition, not a second module-object construction. The arbitrary-site category and all three coefficient specializations, including commutativity and the category instance, are checked in the sandbox scratchpad/ModuleSpecializations.lean through scompile.py. See report for the full clause and universe mapping.
